label: Breitkopf Brahms 1 pp.0-3 — the REACHABLE population, against the print
what: Solo-stem heads (exactly ONE notehead overlaps the stroke) sampled in two strata: MID, where the head sits part-way ALONG the stroke, and END, where it sits at one of its ends. END is the CONTROL: if it cannot be adjudicated either, the crops are measuring the plate and not the rule.
why_this_population: All 44 heads the print has previously adjudicated on this thread have NO overlapping stem in either shared record (the record's own verdict for all 44 is `no_stem`), so no end rule on `_stems_on` can move them. This is the population an end rule CAN move, and it had never been looked at.
blind: Each tile carried an opaque id (T00..T23) and nothing else — no stratum, no direction, no reader's answer. The sheet order was shuffled so position does not encode stratum. Verdicts below were written from the images alone, before the manifest's stratum column was read.
NOT_independent: One adjudicator, and the SAME agent built the crop tool — so this is not an independent eye in the sense an inter-rater figure would give. It is also not independent of the record: the red box IS the record's notehead box, so a tile shows where the pipeline thinks the head is.

verdict_vocabulary.own_stem_at_end: a stroke begins at this head and runs away from it — the engraving convention, satisfied
verdict_vocabulary.mid_stroke: ink runs past the head on BOTH sides; the head is not at an end of the stroke it stands on
verdict_vocabulary.not_a_notehead: the boxed ink is not a notehead at all
verdict_vocabulary.cannot_tell: the adjudicator could not decide from the strip
